title: Informal everyday French
goal: Recognise and use 22 frequent informal words you will hear with friends, in films and on TV.

example.fr: Je n'ai rien pigé à ce film.
example.en: I didn't get that movie at all.

items.note: In Québec, piger usually means “to draw” (a card, a name).

items.en: to fire (from a job), to kick out (informal)

example.fr: Son patron l'a viré la semaine dernière.
example.en: His boss fired him last week.

items.note: In Québec, virer often means “to turn”: virer à gauche.

example.fr: Il est tard, je file !
example.en: It's late, I'm off!

example.fr: Ne traîne pas, on est en retard !
example.en: Don't dawdle, we're late!

example.fr: Tape ton mot de passe et clique sur OK.
example.en: Type your password and click OK.

items.en: to burst, to get a flat (tire)

example.fr: J'ai crevé un pneu sur l'autoroute.
example.en: I got a flat tire on the highway.

items.note: Everyday uses: crever un pneu (to get a flat tire) and je suis crevé (I'm exhausted, informal). Said about a person, crever is a rude way to say “to die”: avoid it.

items.en: to watch out, to be careful (informal)

example.fr: Fais gaffe, la route est glissante !
example.en: Watch out, the road is slippery!

example.fr: Il était complètement bourré à la fête.
example.en: He was completely drunk at the party.

items.note: Informal slang. Neutral words: ivre, soûl.

example.fr: Ce film est complètement débile.
example.en: This movie is totally stupid.

items.note: Informal. Fine about a thing (a film, an idea); said to a person, it is an insult.

example.fr: Tu es cinglé de conduire si vite !
example.en: You're crazy to drive so fast!

example.fr: Ils m'ont proposé un salaire minable.
example.en: They offered me a lousy salary.

example.fr: Mon téléphone est fichu, il ne s'allume plus.
example.en: My phone is done for, it won't turn on anymore.

example.fr: Cette pomme est pourrie, ne la mange pas !
example.en: This apple is rotten, don't eat it!

example.fr: C'est chouette, ton appartement !
example.en: Your apartment is great!

items.note: As a noun, une chouette is an owl.

example.fr: J'ai un rencard avec Lucie samedi.
example.en: I have a date with Lucie on Saturday.

example.fr: Il a passé deux ans en taule.
example.en: He spent two years in prison.

items.note: Slang (also spelled tôle). Neutral word: la prison.

example.fr: Il y a eu une bagarre devant le bar.
example.en: There was a fight in front of the bar.

example.fr: Bonne nuit, fiston !
example.en: Good night, son!

example.fr: Je vais au cinéma avec des copains.
example.en: I'm going to the movies with some friends.

items.note: mon copain / ma copine can also mean my boyfriend / my girlfriend.

example.fr: Elle voit un psy depuis un an.
example.en: She's been seeing a therapist for a year.

example.fr: Il tombe de la flotte depuis ce matin.
example.en: It's been raining since this morning.

example.fr: C'est une nana super sympa.
example.en: She's a really nice girl.

items.note: Informal, mostly heard in France. Neutral words: une fille, une femme.

blocks.title: Usage tips
blocks.body:
These words are **informal**: fine with friends, not in a job interview. [[Bourré]], [[débile]], [[cinglé]], [[taule]] and [[nana]] are slangier. [[Je suis crevé]] = I'm exhausted, but [[crever]] about a person is rude.

**Québec:** [[piger]] = *to draw* (a card), [[virer]] = *to turn*; a boyfriend or girlfriend is [[mon chum]] / [[ma blonde]].

Fais gaffe, la route est glissante !
lines.en: Watch out, the road is slippery!

lines.en: My phone is done for, it won't turn on anymore.

lines.en: I have a date with Lucie on Saturday.

blocks.prompt: In Paris, a friend tells you: “Mon patron m'a viré.” What happened?
options: Their boss gave them a raise.
blocks.explain: In France, [[virer]] (informal) = to fire. In Québec it more often means “to turn”.

blocks.prompt: Which is the informal way to say “Be careful!” to a friend?
blocks.explain: [[Fais gaffe !]] is casual. [[Soyez prudents]] is polite or plural; [[Je vous en prie]] means “you're welcome”.

blocks.prompt: I'm exhausted, I'm going to bed. (man speaking, informal)
accept: Je suis crevé, je vais me coucher.
Je suis crevé, je vais au lit.
Je suis crevé, je me couche.
blocks.explain: [[Je suis crevé]] is the informal way to say “I'm exhausted”.

blocks.prompt: I have a date with Lucie on Saturday. (informal)
accept: J'ai un rencard avec Lucie samedi.
J'ai un rancard avec Lucie samedi.
J'ai un rendez-vous avec Lucie samedi.
J'ai une date avec Lucie samedi.
blocks.explain: [[Un rencard]] is informal for [[un rendez-vous]]. In Québec you will also hear [[une date]].

blocks.text: Cette pomme est ___, ne la mange pas !
blocks.en: This apple is rotten, don't eat it!

blocks.explain: [[Filer]] = to dash off. [[Je traîne]] would mean the opposite: I'm dawdling.

blocks.fr: Je n'ai rien pigé à ce film.
blocks.en: I didn't get that movie at all.
blocks.prompt: What does the speaker say about the movie?

summary:
- Understand casual verbs: [[piger, filer, traîner, faire gaffe]]
- Recognise informal adjectives: [[crevé, bourré, cinglé, fichu, chouette]]
- Know which words differ in Québec ([[piger]], [[virer]], [[chum]] / [[blonde]])
